deepseek.statement: In Gemma 4 E2B, the double-wide MLP in KV-shared layers 25-30 is the main per-position answer-formatting/readout circuit: patching its final-position mlp_out from a correct factual prompt to an incorrect one flips the top-1 answer more than patching equal-width MLP outputs in non-shared layers 0-14 or KV-shared layers 15-20.
deepseek.why_plausible: K-0005 places answer emergence at residual indices 26-34; K-0002 shows layers >=15 can be computed only at the final position; H-001 says layers 15-34 act per-position; H-009 identifies block-25 attention as the subject-to-final transfer. This leaves late per-position MLP as a plausible readout/formatting stage.
competing_explanations: Attention readout at block 25 alone explains the flip, with MLP only amplifying.
The effect is distributed across all late layers rather than localized to layers 25-30.
PLE token-identity injection, not MLP, carries the answer at the final position (H-006).
deepseek.discriminating_experiment: Use 30 factual prompts answered correctly. For each layer 15-34 and a control set 0-14, patch final-position mlp_out from a donor prompt with a different correct answer into the recipient, and measure top-1 flip and logit margin change. Compare to patching attn_out and ple_out at the same layers. Use last_only_from=15 for layers >=15.
deepseek.numeric_prediction: Supports if patching mlp_out at layers 25-30 flips top-1 in >50% of prompts and changes the target-answer logit by >2.0, while layers 15-20 and 0-14 flip <10%; refutes if flips are uniform across layers or <20% at layers 25-30.
deepseek.novelty_risk: Late-layer MLP readout is consistent with logit-lens dynamics in other LMs and may already be shown by standard MLP patching; the KV-shared double-wide localization is the novel part.

deepseek.area: knowledge storage & retrieval (facts vs context vs association)
deepseek.statement: Parametric factual recall and in-context associative recall in E2B share the layer-13 K/V -> block-25 extraction route, but parametric facts additionally require late PLE token-identity injection, whereas in-context associations can be retrieved without it.
deepseek.why_plausible: H-008 shows subject info reaches the final position via layer-13 sliding K/V; H-009 shows block-25 attention is the transfer site; H-006 proposes PLE lets late layers re-read token identity. K-0005 shows late answer emergence, consistent with a late PLE-dependent readout for parametric facts.
competing_explanations: In-context associations also require PLE, so PLE is a general late readout mechanism.
Parametric facts are stored in MLP weights and do not depend on layer-13 K/V; the KV route is only for context.
Both fact types use layer-14 full K/V rather than layer-13 sliding K/V.
deepseek.discriminating_experiment: Build 20 parametric fact prompts and 20 in-context association prompts with matched answer tokens. For each, replace layer-13 K/V (and separately layer-14 K/V) for layers 15-34 with donor K/V, and ablate PLE injection at layers 15-34. Measure answer accuracy and logit margin.
deepseek.numeric_prediction: Supports if layer-13 K/V replacement drops both prompt types by >0.5 accuracy, PLE ablation drops parametric accuracy by >0.5 but in-context by <0.1, and layer-14 replacement drops <0.2 for short prompts; refutes if PLE ablation affects both equally or layer-14 replacement dominates.
deepseek.novelty_risk: PLE role is already H-006; in-context vs parametric retrieval differences are known in other LMs, but the shared layer-13 route is architecture-specific.

deepseek.statement: E2B generalizes factual recall across paraphrased templates through the same layer-13 K/V subject representation, but fails to transfer to novel entity-relation combinations because block-25 attention binds only relation-specific subject directions seen during pretraining.
deepseek.why_plausible: H-008 and H-009 give a concrete subject-to-final route; K-0005 shows late answer emergence; H-012 suggests multi-token subject information is spread in layer-13 K/V. This predicts template invariance if the subject K/V direction is stable, but relation-specific failure if the binding is memorized.
competing_explanations: Paraphrase generalization is mediated by PLE token identity rather than layer-13 K/V.
Novel relation combinations succeed because block-25 attention implements a general relation-binding algorithm.
Memorization is localized in MLP weights, so K/V replacement should not affect paraphrase transfer.
deepseek.discriminating_experiment: Create 15 known facts in canonical and 3 paraphrases each, plus 15 novel relation-entity combinations using the same relation words. Measure accuracy, then replace layer-13 K/V from canonical to paraphrase and from known to novel prompts; also measure block-25 attention to subject tokens.
deepseek.numeric_prediction: Supports if paraphrase accuracy is >80% and layer-13 K/V replacement preserves >70% of paraphrase answers, while novel-combination accuracy is <20% and its layer-13 K/V causal effect is <0.2; refutes if novel-combination accuracy is >50% or paraphrase depends on PLE rather than K/V.
deepseek.novelty_risk: Paraphrase robustness and relation-specific recall are studied in other LMs; the KV-sharing route and block-25 binding are the novel claims.

deepseek.area: computational efficiency without quality loss (prefill, decode, KV cache, precision)
deepseek.statement: The exact last_only_from=15 optimization extends to batched KV-cache decode: for prompts <=512 tokens, computing layers 15-34 only for the newly decoded final query position at each step yields identical next-token logits to full computation, because non-final positions after layer 14 are causally inert.
deepseek.why_plausible: K-0001 shows non-final positions entering layers 15/16/25/34 are causally inert for final-position logits; K-0002 shows last_only_from=15 reproduces full-sequence final-position logits and cuts CPU time; H-001 states layers 15-34 act per-position. The untested part is batched KV-cache decode.
competing_explanations: KV-cache decode changes the effective attention mask or position handling, so the optimization is not exact under generation.
Batched sequences interact through padding or cache layout, causing logit drift even if single-sequence is exact.
The optimization is exact only for prefill, not for autoregressive decode.
deepseek.discriminating_experiment: Take 20 prompts of 12-30 tokens. Run full batched generation for 8 new tokens and a modified runner that computes layers 15-34 only for the current final position per decode step, using kv_store for layers 13/14. Compare next-token logits and top-1 at every step.
deepseek.numeric_prediction: Supports if max |Δlogit| <1e-4 and top-1 agreement is 100% across all steps and prompts; refutes if max |Δlogit| >0.01 or top-1 agreement <95% on any step.
deepseek.novelty_risk: K-0002 already shows single-sequence final-position exactness; batched KV-cache decode is the untested extension, but similar per-position optimizations may exist in inference engines.

deepseek.statement: Editing a factual association by replacing layer-13 K/V at the subject token changes the answer with high specificity, but produces more interference on same-relation facts than editing late final-position MLP/residual states, because layer-13 K/V is shared by all later layers and relation templates.
deepseek.why_plausible: H-008 identifies layer-13 K/V as the subject-information route; H-009 identifies block-25 attention as the transfer site; H-002's ROME two-site pattern suggests mid-layer subject and late final-token sites. KV sharing means a layer-13 edit is reused by layers 15-34, predicting broad but relation-coupled effects.
competing_explanations: Late MLP/residual edits cause more interference because they affect answer formatting globally.
Layer-13 K/V edits are highly specific because they only affect the edited subject token, not relation templates.
Interference is dominated by PLE token-identity injection rather than K/V or MLP.
deepseek.discriminating_experiment: Select 10 facts in one relation (e.g., country->capital). Edit fact A to a new answer by replacing layer-13 K/V at the subject token with donor K/V, and separately by patching final-position mlp_out/resid_post at layers 25-30. Measure edit success on A and interference on the other 9 same-relation facts plus 10 unrelated facts.
deepseek.numeric_prediction: Supports if layer-13 K/V edit success is >0.8 and same-relation interference is >0.3, while late MLP/residual edit success is >0.6 and same-relation interference is <0.1; refutes if both edit types show similar interference or layer-13 edits are <0.5 successful.
deepseek.novelty_risk: ROME-style editing and interference are well studied; the KV-sharing-specific prediction that layer-13 edits are reused by 20 layers is novel.

deepseek.area: confidence / calibration / error detection from internals
deepseek.statement: For factual prompts in E2B, the layer-28 logit-lens margin and block-25 attention entropy are better error detectors than final softmax confidence, because answer emergence occurs at residual indices 26-34 and subject-to-final transfer is concentrated in block 25.
deepseek.why_plausible: K-0005 shows the correct answer first becomes top-1 at residual index 26-34 (median 28); H-009 shows block-25 attention is the subject-to-final transfer site; H-010 suggests head 25.0 is dominant. These internal signals should separate correct from incorrect recalls before final calibration.
competing_explanations: Final softmax confidence already captures all available uncertainty, so internal margins add nothing.
Errors are caused by PLE token-identity failures, so PLE gate norms rather than attention entropy predict errors.
Attention entropy is uninformative because block-25 attention is diffuse even on correct prompts.
deepseek.discriminating_experiment: Collect 100 factual prompts with known answers, including 30 likely errors. Compute final softmax confidence, layer-28 logit-lens margin, block-25 attention entropy, and PLE gate norm at the final position. Evaluate AUROC for predicting correctness and calibration error.
deepseek.numeric_prediction: Supports if layer-28 margin AUROC >0.75 and block-25 entropy AUROC >0.65, while final confidence AUROC <0.65; refutes if final confidence is the best detector (AUROC >0.75) or internal signals are <=0.6.
deepseek.novelty_risk: Logit-lens and attention-entropy confidence are known in other LMs; the specific layer-28/block-25 combination in a KV-shared model is novel.

deepseek.area: radically new principle for discovering regularities beyond hypothesis enumeration
deepseek.statement: The effective final-position computation of E2B is low-dimensional in the layer-13/14 K/V subspace: unsupervised PCA/ridge on layer-13/14 K/V across diverse prompts recovers axes that predict answer category, correctness, and template without enumerating circuits, because all cross-position information reaching the final position is carried by those K/V tensors.
deepseek.why_plausible: K-0001 and H-001 state all cross-position information reaching the final position is carried by layer-13/14 K/V; K-0002 shows final-position computation can be isolated; H-008 and H-009 identify layer-13 K/V and block-25 attention as the main route. This makes the K/V subspace a natural low-dimensional causal state for discovery.
competing_explanations: The K/V subspace is high-dimensional and no low-dimensional axes predict behavior better than random projections.
Final-position residual/PLE, not K/V, carries most predictable variance.
Answer category and correctness are encoded in attention patterns rather than K/V content.
deepseek.discriminating_experiment: Collect 200 diverse prompts (facts, paraphrases, in-context associations, errors). Extract layer-13 and layer-14 K/V at the subject and final positions. Fit PCA and ridge regression (CPU, no SAE) to predict answer token category, correctness, and template from 1-50 components. Compare to random projections and to final residual/PLE features.
deepseek.numeric_prediction: Supports if 20 PCA components of layer-13/14 K/V predict answer category with >70% accuracy and correctness with AUROC >0.7, versus <40% and <0.6 for random projections; refutes if K/V features do not beat random projections or final residual/PLE by a meaningful margin.
deepseek.novelty_risk: Linear probing and PCA of K/V are standard; the principle that the KV-shared subspace is the sufficient low-dimensional state for discovery is novel but may overlap with existing representation-probing work.
